steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, green onion, sugar, garlic, sesame seeds, sesame oil, and pepper together in a bowl.
Place flank steak slices in a shallow dish. Pour marinade over top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Quickly grill flank steak slices on the preheated grill until slightly charred and cooked through, 1 to 2 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Bulgogi
raw_recipe.description: Our best bulgogi recipe uses a sweet soy and sesame marinade. Also known as Korean BBQ beef, this thinly sliced grilled steak is easy to make at home.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make bulgogi, sometimes known as Korean BBQ beef, the perfect dish for your next outdoor cookout. The thinly sliced grilled steak marinated in a sweet soy, sesame, and garlic sauce cooks quickly on the grill, so don’t wander off too far. Garnish the platter with green onions and sesame seeds, or make a meal out of this recipe by serving the strips in lettuce cups with rice and hot pepper paste.

review.reviewBody: This is the same recipe I have used for years. We love it. The only thing I do different is I use 2 1/2 tablespoons brown sugar instead of white sugar. The same amount. Try it you will like it. My son makes excellent Bulgogi and egg rolls. This is the recipe that we use. We buy a good beef loin and freeze it. That makes it easier to slice. He slices it very thin and then we marinate. We also use this marinade on chicken and pork. It is delicious.

Great flavor! I double the sauce and one batch is flank steak and the other chopped boneless skinless chicken thighs and marinade both overnight. I spread each meat separately in a baking pan lined with parchment paper and cook at 350 for 15 minutes then switch to broiler for 5 minutes or until meat has a little singe. I put either meat in a French roll or flour tortilla with mayo, mustard, pickles lettuce and cheese. Keep the meats separate and sealed in the fridge and heat as needed. I hear about 1 cup of meat for 2min 30 sec on 50% in the microwave. I’m single so this lasts me all week.

Really good! Kids even loved it. I followed the suggestion to substitute brown sugar. I marinated the beef for about 7 hours. I had to cook inside so I put the pan on high/sear setting and laid pieces down flat and flipped after a minute or less to keep from over-cooking. Used egg noodles because that’s what I had- butter, sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic, salt, & pepper to taste on the noodles, along with sautéed broccolini.
Made this a few times. Only thing I have changed is I grate 1/4 of an onion into the marinade. I add sliced onions, peppers and mushrooms when I cook this in a wok, but prefer it over fire

great flavor! I found that I had about 1/2 of the green onion in the recipe - I substituted dried onion as it was for the marinade. I used dark soy sauce as that is all I had, but I did not grill - rather cooked in a high heat wok so I think the dark soy sauce worked to my advantage. Meat when finished was an awesome "grilled" color. Used dark brown sugar, but any sugar helps with caramelization. 
Lastly, there was a lot of tasty bits when the meat was done so I added approx 1/4 cup of water which instantly made an awesome sauce and then threw in some fresh spinach I had to add veggies. Wilted spinach and tossed with tongs in the sauce - took 30-45 seconds. I think you could do this with any favorite veggie you have. Served over Bob's Mill organic brown basmati rice.

Great recipe. Recently I made a variation: sliced chuck roast, tough cut, I know. After marinating overnight, I put meat and marinade in my pressure cooker for 30 minutes on high pressure. (mine is electric) added some carrots too along with some corn starch slurry. The best stew EVER!

This recipe is so bomb! I was trying to recreate a burrito from one of my favorite restaurants that closed, this bulgogi recipe was spot on. 
I made a couple adjustments from reading other reviews. I froze the meat for a half hour which made it very easy to slice thin, I used brown sugar instead of white and also cooked it over the stove top on high heat. Marinated the meat for 6 hours. 

I put this in a warm tortilla along with lime and cilantro infused rice, diced onions, lettuce, kimchi and of course the bulgogi. I also drizzled some of the marinade over the meat after. My husband had TWO freaking burritos! Next time I will try it with a fried egg and avocado. This is definitely going to be one of my staple recipes. Thank you!!

This was delicious, although it doesn't really taste like any Bulgogi I've had before. I think next time I make it I'll leave out the sesame seeds and just sprinkle them on top. I also think I'll scale back just a bit on the garlic as it was strong. I did add 1/2 a grated pear to help to tenderize the meat. I wasn't able to grill the meat so I cooked it on the stove in a fry pan and once cooked there was a lot of liquid so I made a slurry of cornstarch/soy sauce/water and drizzled it in. It turned the liquid into a wonderful gravy. Will definitely make again!

So good! I made some changes though. I used a tablespoon of brown sugar instead of white. I pureed half a pear, a small piece of fresh ginger, 4 garlic cloves, the soy sauce and sesame oil. After that was blended I added the green onion, red pepper flakes and black pepper. I let it marinate for about 30 minutes. I don't have a bbq so the meat was cooked in batches on the stove. It was so good! I stir fried sliced zucchini, red onion, mushrooms and green onion for the side and some plain white rice. This recipe is a keeper!

Swapped the white sugar with brown sugar, used sliced Kobe beef, added onions and red bell peppers, and cooked it on a cast iron skillet instead of the grill (it's winter in Wisconsin) - me and my friends loved it! I don't cook a lot and this was my first time doing both a marinade and beef dish, but my friends couldn't stop raving about it. It's very, very flavorful and can be eaten all on its own without any rice (I actually think the rice dilutes the flavor).

I've been making this for years now, my family loves this! I have a grill pan that I use on the stovetop when the weather isn't good for grilling outside and either way it turns out great. Freeze for about 30 min before slicing and double the sauce. Serve with steamed rice, green lettuce and julienned carrots, cucumbers and bell pepper to create lettuce wraps. Or just eat on its own!

We had 2# of stew meat to use up, so I made this recipe, left the meat in the marinade in the frig for 24 hours, cooked it on "simmer" in cast iron, then we mixed it with steamed broccoli to imitate a menu item from a Chinese restaurant. We loved it!
Will make again. Followed a reviewer and baked 15 minutes at 350, then broiled 5 minutes.

We love Asian food, and this tasted better than the most upscale Korean restaurant in town!! I used flat iron steak instead of flank steak, and I doubled the ingredients for the sauce as that's just our preference. I added broccoli, snap peas, julienne carrots, water chestnuts, bok choy, and a thinly sliced red bell pepper, but I think any vegetable would work depending on your preferences. I also used brown sugar for the marinade, and a sweet Vidalia onion instead of green onions. I served it with basmati rice and sautéed green beans and garlic. My family went nuts over this, and asked me to make this meal once a week. I highly recommend giving this recipe a try!!
Excellent, made it several times
She loved it!

I had to make three changes, but it turned out great. Mine didn't taste quite like the Bulgogi I enjoyed while teaching in S. Korea, but I knew why. First, brown sugar instead of white was a deliberate choice. Second, I had no Soy Sauce, but All Recipes had suggestions! I substituted Worcestershire Sauce. With no green onions, I used white onions that were on hand. My wife took one taste and said, "Don't lose that recipe; I want more soon!"

this is one of my favorites to have for summer - put on top of cabbage, spinach, and romaine- make up a aïoli sauce. Right now I’m trying to get rid of my basic ranch so I add ranch, Dijon mustard &Sriracha & pepper, oh and a little lime or lemon juice!!!!

My Family and I LOVED this recipe! I made it just the way the recipe follows, but tweaked a few things. I Love onions, but not everyone in my family does, so I thinly sliced a small shallot and used that instead of a sweet onion. I used brown sugar because we don’t use white sugar in my household. I just made sure I mixed it perfectly! I marinated the Strip Steak in a bag with the marinade I made from the ingredients for 30 mins before I cooked it, and it turned out Awesome!! I made Basmati rice, we had Romain lettuce for Bulgogi rolls, and also a side of Korean Steamed Buns( HEB) We all added the Kimchi (bought from Costco), and it was Delish!! I will probably make this twice a month from now on!
Thought it would be tough to make, but really wasnt! Tasted great!
